$comment: Reviewed inputs to the app's third-party notices -- #664. scripts/check-third-party-notices.mjs reads this file; nothing else does.
noLicenceFile: packages in the app's distributed closure whose installed tarball carries NO licence file. The generator fails closed on
such a package unless an entry here, keyed by name@version, says where its notice comes from instead. A version bump therefore fails
closed again until somebody re-reads the new version. 'excerpt' is read from a file INSIDE the installed package; 'upstream' is text
read from the project's own repository at a named commit, because the package carries none at all. 'licenceText' adds the licence's
canonical text, which this repository already pins (LIC005). copiedIntoBuild: files the build copies verbatim out of a package into dist,
named so the notice says which package each came from.

writtenByTheBundler: packages whose OWN code the bundler writes into dist, which no closure lists because they are build tools -- see WRITTEN_BY_THE_BUNDLER in the generator. Keyed by the INSTALLED name@version, so a bump fails closed (NOT008). 'files' are read verbatim from the installed package; 'from'/'through' cut a file down to the part that covers the code that ships.

A copiedIntoBuild entry may carry 'vendored' (#618): the copied file is somebody else's work that its package vendors -- Binomial's Apache-2.0 transcoder inside the MIT three -- so its notice is written here, once per work, because the package's own licence field cannot say it.

@mediapipe/tasks-vision@1.0.1.why: The tarball holds its bundles, its types and its WebAssembly and no LICENSE. Its manifest says Apache-2.0, and its type declarations open with the project's Apache-2.0 header, which is the notice it does ship.

murmurhash-js@1.0.0.why: The tarball holds no LICENSE file; its README ends with the MIT licence and its copyright line, which is the notice it does ship.

pmtiles@4.5.0.why: The tarball holds its source, its build and its README and no licence text at all. The text below is the repository's own LICENSE at the commit that released js v4.5.0 (its message ends 'js v4.5.0'), byte-identical to the file at the repository's HEAD on the day it was read.

vendored.name: Basis Universal transcoder
vendored.what: basis_transcoder.js and basis_transcoder.wasm, in realistic/basis/: the transcoder of Basis Universal v1.50, by Binomial LLC, as three 0.185.1 vendors it under examples/jsm/libs/basis/ (three.js took v1.50 in mrdoob/three.js#29418, its last change to these files). The realistic world's KTX2 textures are transcoded by it, on the device, to the GPU's own block formats. The WebAssembly has Zstandard's decoder compiled in, under BSD-3-Clause, which is how it reads a UASTC texture's Zstandard supercompression. Upstream v1.50 carries no NOTICE file (one was added in February 2026, after this version), so Apache-2.0 section 4(d) asks for none; the copy of the licence section 4(a) asks for is the appendix. three's own licence field says MIT and cannot say any of this, which is why it is written here.
